title: IPO-Bound Jio Platforms Reports 9 Percent Profit Growth to Rs 7,764 Crore in Q1

body:
Jio Posts Solid Quarter Ahead of Mega IPO

IPO-bound Jio Platforms reported a consolidated profit after tax of Rs 7,764 crore in Q1 FY27, up 9.2 percent year-over-year, as it prepares for what could be India's largest-ever tech listing.

Operating revenue rose 11.8 percent to Rs 39,173 crore, while EBITDA grew 15.1 percent to Rs 20,865 crore. EBITDA margin expanded 150 basis points year-over-year to 53.3 percent, reflecting improving operational efficiency.

533 Million Subscribers and Counting

Jio ended the quarter with more than 533 million subscribers, including approximately 285 million 5G users. Fixed broadband connections reached 29 million, of which 14 million were JioAirFiber homes. Data traffic surged 26.9 percent year-over-year to 69.4 exabytes, with average monthly data consumption reaching 43.7 GB per user.

Average revenue per user ticked up to Rs 215.6 per month from Rs 208.8 a year earlier. Digital services revenue grew 20 percent, outpacing connectivity, with content, cloud compute, IoT, and managed services driving growth.

The IPO That NRI Investors Are Watching

Jio filed its DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of 27 crore shares, eyeing to raise approximately $4 billion (around Rs 34,000 crore). Of the proceeds, Rs 27,500 crore will prepay borrowings, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes.

"As we embark on our next phase to be a publicly listed company, we will continue to maintain our deep tech focus and democratise access to digital connectivity in India and globally," said managing director Akash Ambani.

Reliance Industries holds a 66.43 percent stake, while Meta owns 9.98 percent and Google holds 7.73 percent — making the Jio IPO a convergence point for some of the world's biggest tech investors.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI investors, Jio's IPO represents one of the most significant opportunities to invest in India's digital infrastructure. The company's reach touches virtually every Indian household — from mobile connectivity to streaming entertainment to broadband — making it one of the few IPOs where investors have a deeply personal understanding of the product.

Parent Reliance Industries reported overall Q1 net profit of Rs 23,001 crore, up 5.7 percent year-over-year, with gross revenue rising 24.5 percent to Rs 3.40 lakh crore.

Sources: Inc42, Reliance Industries Q1 FY27 disclosures
nri_angle: Jio's IPO is one of the most watched by NRI investors, and its 533 million subscriber base includes family connections relevant to the diaspora.
